From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T17:15:00-07:00
Subject: We missed you on today's office hours — reschedule & quick help

Hi Samir —

We had the office hours scheduled for today at 11:00am PT but it looks like you couldn't make it. No problem — I know things come up. I wanted to follow up with a quick checklist that often fixes the 401 error folks hit on day one, and propose a couple of makeup slots:

Quick checklist (most common fixes):
- Confirm the API key was copied from the dashboard (no leading/trailing spaces)
- Ensure the key is set in REDWOOD_API_KEY or passed in x-redwood-api-key header
- Confirm environment (dev vs prod) — keys are environment-scoped in the trial
- If using the SDK, run the provided "configure.sh" in sdk-quickstart.zip to write credentials

Proposed slots for a 30-min follow-up:
- Tue Apr 20, 10:00–10:30am PT
- Wed Apr 21, 2:30–3:00pm PT

If neither works, happy to do an async debugging session — you can paste the short request/response (with the key redacted) into the session-log-template.csv and I'll take a look.

Also attaching a simple session-log-template.csv you can fill in.

If you'd like to try one quick thing right now: run the curl from the attached curl-sample.txt and paste the full HTTP response (headers + body) — that usually gives us the error code and request_id to trace on our side.

Best,
Marcus

Attachment: session-log-template.csv (text/csv)

From: Samir Patel <samir@acmerobotics.com>

Subject: Re: We missed you on today's office hours — reschedule & quick help

Hi Marcus —

Apologies — an ops incident at Acme pulled us into triage and I couldn't step away. I really appreciate the follow-up and the checklist.

We tried the API key from the dashboard and immediately got a 401. Here's the response we saw (sanitized):

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 18:07:32 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Request-Id: r-0f93a2b7

{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or inactive"}

We copied the key into REDWOOD_API_KEY and retried. No host-header rewriting or proxy on our side — straight POST to https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate.

I can do the Tue Apr 20 10:00am PT slot if that still works, otherwise Wed afternoon would be fine.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Robotics
samir@acmerobotics.com

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the details and the request_id — that's exactly what we need to trace this.

Two quick things we can validate before the call to speed up debugging:
1) Can you confirm the trial API key status in the dashboard (this is under Account > API keys) — is it marked "Active"? If you can't access the dashboard, send the key id (not the secret) and we can check on our side.
2) If you're hitting our API through any internal gateway, please confirm the Host header is api.redwood.com and no additional auth proxy is stripping the header.

I've also attached a minimal curl sample (curl-sample.txt) that hits the same endpoint we use for the SDK — if you run it and paste the response we'll get an immediate trace.

I can take the Tue Apr 20, 10:00–10:30am PT slot with Marcus. If you'd prefer Wed Apr 21, Evelyn can take the 2:30–3:00pm PT slot instead. Let me know which you'd prefer and I'll send a refreshed calendar invite.

If it's easier, we can also do a 20-min recorded screenshare — you can share your terminal and we'll walk through the key setup.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
